§1 — What the machine description already gives, and what it lacks

The S1 plans model each supply into its own coil. An integrated test of the supplies needs the rest of the electromagnetic system: every coil's coupling to every other coil and to the vacuum vessel, and the circuits that connect supplies to coils. This plan builds that system from the IDS machine description, so the same code runs on any machine that publishes one, ITER included.

imas-ambix already authors a JT-60SA machine description per operating phase (~/Code/imas-ambix/maps/jt-60sa/machine_description/OP1 and OP2, Data Dictionary 4.1.1) with five IDSs: magnetics, pf_active, pf_passive, tf and wall. A prototype run against OP2 found:

ContentState in the OP2 store
Coils12: CS1–4 (40 elements, 549 turns each), EF1–6 (16 elements, 142–353 turns), FPPC_UP and FPPC_DOWN (6 elements, 23 turns)
Passive structures2 loops; the vacuum vessel has 98 elements (63 in OP1)
Suppliesnone
Coil resistanceempty
Circuits12 placeholders, one per coil, each a 1 × 1 "connection" holding the coil index. The Data Dictionary requires 2 × (supplies + coils) columns, and nova rejects them

nova computes the coil-coil inductance matrix from this description (scripts/jt60sa/machine_description.py, run in nova's environment): 76 s on a CPU, symmetric to 2 × 10⁻¹⁰, with self-inductances of 375 mH (EF5) to 716 mH (EF6) and 289.5 mH for each CS module. Two adaptations were needed. nova's reader expects the DD3 coil.identifier, so the IDS is converted to DD 3.42 first, and the placeholder circuits are cleared.

The 2021 single-coil tests already measure these couplings. In each test one booster drives its coil and the neighbours pick up its ripple; for an open neighbour with nothing in between, the ratio of their coil-voltage lines is M/L. The measured 6f ratios are below nova's M/L for every pair: by 1.3 times for neighbours such as EF5 and EF6, and by up to 14 times for distant pairs such as EF5 and EF2. That is the signature of screening by the passive structures, and it is the first test the model has to pass.

Measured across frequency, the same tests settle the geometry. At 0.12–0.24 Hz the pickup ratio equals nova's M/L within 2–8 % for all nine pairs with long records (coherence ≥ 0.98), so the machine description and nova are right at DC, and the deficit at 6f is frequency-dependent screening, characterised in §5.

Two features of the same data will need explaining. The ratios fall further at 12f and 18f (EF5 to EF6: 0.39, 0.13, 0.11), as screening predicts. EF6's pickup arrives near 180° when EF5 or EF2 drives, while every other pair but EF5 to CS4 (62°) is within 20° of zero. Either EF6's turns or its voltage channel carries the opposite sign to the description, or EF6's circuit responds differently. The low-frequency ratios taken over the swing are also below M/L, which a neighbour supply holding its current would explain.

§2 — The circuits as built

Establish every circuit that connects a supply to a coil, and whether any circuit links several coils. What is known so far:

  • Each of the ten superconducting coils has its own circuit: a base supply, in series with a booster (EF1, EF2, EF5, EF6) or a switching network unit (CS1–4, EF3, EF4), and a quench protection circuit. The booster circuits carry the ripple filter, and every circuit the alternative grounding (jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence §2, §6).
  • The two fast plasma position control coils inside the vessel are each fed by their own converter: a four-quadrant, twelve-pulse thyristor converter with circulating current, ±1 kV and ±5 kA, with a crowbar and a non-linear resistor across the coil against disruption overvoltages of up to 10 kV. The vertical-stability function is therefore a control coupling of two independent circuits, unless the documents show the converters wired together.
  • The eighteen sector coils of the resistive-wall-mode system (about 300 A and 240 V each) are non-axisymmetric and outside this plan.

The data can test the circuit topology directly. Coils in one series circuit carry one current, and coils in anti-series carry opposite currents. The channels are on disk: the fast-control-coil currents, supply voltages and references, and the dump-resistor voltages of every coil, for all 52 shots, in data/jt60sa/nodes/ (scripts/jt60sa/fetch_circuit_nodes.py); the switching-unit terminal voltages are in the main shot files. The fast-control coils carry no current in any 2023 shot (E100963 to E101090), consistent with their completion in December 2025, so the 2023 data hold the ten PF circuits only. Test every PF coil pair for current identity.

Done when a circuit table in this plan cites a source for each circuit's elements and connection, and the current-identity test has run over every coil pair in the 2023 plasma shots with its result recorded. Positive control: a synthetic anti-series pair built from one coil's current and its negative is detected. Negative control: CS1 and CS2, which have separate supplies, are not.

§3 — Channel signs and the EF6 phase

A coil channel's sign decides whether a pickup arrives at 0° or 180°, so it has to be known before the pickup can test the model. For each coil, regress its slow coil voltage on the L dI/dt formed from its own current over a swing, with L from the §1 matrix: the sign of the slope is the channel's sign relative to the machine description's turns. Then settle EF6's 180° pickup, by a channel sign or by the state of EF6's circuit while its neighbours are driven. booster-converter-model's measurement-chain section can take the same sign table.

The regression extends the slow balance that exists rather than adding another: circuit.py's filtered derivative, swing selection and self/mutual regression (identify_split, with its 2 Hz balance filter), and the dump-voltage regression in scripts/jt60sa/fast_discharge_couplings.py. The table then becomes the one sign policy. It replaces the shot-dependent EF6 correction in scripts/figures/jt60sa_measured_couplings.py now, and the inferred sign in scripts/figures/jt60sa_coupling_transfer.py when that script is consolidated after §5. Its surface is one module holding the table and a lookup by coil and shot.

The data already narrow it. EF6's pickup is inverted in every shot up to E100329, whichever coil drives (EF5, EF2, and the CS1 and CS2 fast discharges), with the magnitude of M/L, and it is correct in every shot from E100347 on. EF6's own fast discharge E100346 still reads inverted: its self-inductance comes out at −691 mH against nova's 716 mH, and every pickup has the opposite sign. Something in EF6's channel or connection changed between E100346 and E100347.

Done when a sign table for the ten coils and the two fast-control coils is recorded in this plan with the shots it used, and EF6's phase is either explained by it or left open with the evidence. Positive control: a channel inverted on purpose is reported with the opposite sign. Negative control: a coil with no excitation in the window, its own dI/dt below a threshold declared before the run so the regressor has no rank, is reported as unidentifiable with no sign rather than as a measured zero slope. The unexcited fast-control coils are reported the same way.

§4 — Supplies and circuits in the machine description

Write the §2 circuits into a pf_active overlay on the ambix geometry: a new module src/power_convertor/coil_system.py reads the ambix store with imas-python, adds one supply per converter (base, booster, switching network unit, fast-control-coil converter) with its voltage and current limits, writes each circuit as a connection matrix of the size the Data Dictionary defines, adds coil resistances where a document gives them, and saves the result under data/jt60sa/machine_description/. Every value cites its source in the module. The overlay is a candidate for imas-ambix's own store, offered there once it is checked; the geometry stays ambix's.

The module's public surface is one builder that returns the overlay and one writer that saves it. It takes over the Data Dictionary conversion from scripts/jt60sa/machine_description.py, which then calls it and stops clearing the circuits, so there is one conversion path. Nothing else is retired, because no existing module writes supplies or circuits.

Done when nova builds the overlay's circuits without error, and tests/test_coil_system.py shows that each single-coil circuit's current equals its coil's current. Negative control: the ambix placeholder circuits are refused by the same loader with the column-count error the prototype met.

§5 — The coupling transfer functions, characterised from data

Modelling the vessel and the other passive conductors from their geometry and resistivity is possible but slow to get right, and it is not needed to use the coupling. The 2021 single-coil tests measure the coupling transfer function H(f) = Vpickup/Vdriven directly: from 0.1 to 30 Hz over the swing, by cross-spectral estimate, and at the converter harmonics 6f to 18f over the hold, as complex line ratios (scripts/figures/jt60sa_coupling_transfer.py, results in data/jt60sa/coupling_transfer.json).

At the lowest frequencies H is nova's M/L. Below 30 Hz it falls with two time constants shared by every pair, 151 ms and 42 ms, with a weight per pair, to 4.6 % rms of M/L. Shared time constants are what eigenmodes of the passive structure produce, so the screening points to a few passive loops whose couplings to the coils are identified rather than computed. The measured H is a ratio of terminal voltages, not a coupling. A passive loop also screens the driven coil's own impedance, so H carries a denominator that depends on the driven coil, and its pole weights do not factorise directly into one coupling per coil. The loops are therefore fitted through the coupled circuit equations of coils and loops, which give H for an open pickup coil with the driven coil's self-screening included. If the loops are physical, their couplings fitted on some pairs predict the others. That is the test this section runs. The converter harmonics sit two to five times above the fitted high-frequency gain, a separate effect this section characterises at the line frequencies; the pickups' own supplies are off in those tests, so the lines are coupling. One ratio exceeds M/L: EF5 to EF4 at 12f is 0.57 against a DC M/L of 0.288. A purely inductive network with passive loops can exceed the DC ratio (a positive-definite three-coil example gives 0.33 against 0.2), so the excess does not by itself show a common-mode or capacitive path through the grounding. Both explanations are kept as hypotheses, and the coupled-circuit fit says whether the inductive one suffices.

Further excitations widen the data: the 2023 single-coil tests at two hold currents, the plasma-campaign shots in which several supplies run, and any coil fast discharge into its quench-protection dump resistor, whose exponential current decay excites every frequency the swing does not. The dump-resistor voltages <coil>/volQPCDR identify those discharges.

The 2021 shot log names sixteen of them, covering every coil but EF2: CS1 E100247, E100253, E100256, E100325 and E100326; CS2 E100329; CS3 E100333; CS4 E100336; EF3 E100343; EF4 E100289, E100290, E100294 and E100339; EF5 E100276; EF6 E100346; EF1 E100352. Each dump puts about 0.168 Ω across the coil. From the March 2021 dumps one event gives a whole coupling row within a few percent of nova's M/L (CS1 to CS2 0.209 against 0.215, CS1 to EF3 0.143 against 0.149, CS2 to EF5 0.029 against 0.028), and the coil's own voltage against dI/dt gives its self-inductance without the dump resistance (CS1 286 mH and CS2 275 mH against nova's 289 mH). In the February CS1 dumps (E100247 to E100256) the neighbour voltage channels hold fixed offsets with no pickup, so those shots give the self-inductance only. The fast ramps of CS2 and EF5 to ±5 kA (E100268, E100269, E100277, E100278) are a further excitation.

A scan of every shot's dump-resistor voltages (scripts/jt60sa/scan_fast_discharges.py, catalogued by scripts/jt60sa/fast_discharge_catalogue.py into data/jt60sa/fast_discharge_catalogue.json) finds 213 shots with dumps from 2021 to 2023: 146 in which a single coil dumps, with 10 to 22 for every coil including EF2 (E100319, E100320, E100444, E100445, E100448, E100449, E100497, E100498, E100911, E100912, E101134), at 1, 3 and 5 kA, and 67 in which several dump together. The 2023 single-coil dumps (E100884 to E101134) measure the couplings after the filters and the grounding changed.

The seven March 2021 dumps whose neighbour channels are live, with the booster tests' lowest frequencies, already give the DC coupling matrix: 62 dump pairs and 11 swing pairs sit around nova's M/L with medians of 0.955 and 0.989, and seven coils' self-inductances lie within 1–7 % of nova's (EF4 605–624 mH against 629 mH, EF1 538 against 551, EF3 339 against 332).

Two owners already exist and are extended rather than copied. The complex line ratio is circuit.pickup_ratio, which locks the frequency for each harmonic. The estimators copied into scripts/figures/jt60sa_coil_coupling.py and jt60sa_coupling_transfer.py reuse the 6f lock for every order, and only one applies a line threshold. pickup_ratio gains the threshold as an optional argument and both scripts move onto it, so the catalogue and §6 use one estimator. The identified loops are held as physical circuit elements, each loop's resistance and self-inductance and its mutual inductance to each coil, which is the form nova's passive model holds (nova/circuit/passive.py). They can then be compared with nova's own pf_passive loops and enter §6's state equations directly. Identifying them from data is the new work. The new surface is one module, coupling_modes.py, with a fit and a prediction, and the per-pair fit in the figure script is retired in its favour.

The first model has been measured, and it fails. Free passive loops, each with its own resistance, self-inductance and mutual inductance to every coil, fit the training pairs to 3–6 %. Under leave-one-pair-out cross-validation they miss the 10 % band on all nine measured EF pairs (14.9–825 % of M/L), and beat M/L alone on six of them. Their fitted decay times, 0.076, 0.101 and 0.218 s, lie inside the range of nova's own passive eigenmodes for the OP2 vessel and cryostat (0.064–0.218 s). The fit, its cross-validation table and nova's eigenmodes are recorded in the jccm-modes fragment, produced by scripts/jt60sa/passive_loops_fit.py and scripts/jt60sa/nova_passive_modes.py. On 2026-10-13 the lead chose the next model: nova's geometry-derived passive structure from pf_passive, with only physical scales fitted, the vessel and cryostat resistivities, on the same training pairs and through the same coupled-circuit terminal ratio. It is scored on the same held-out pairs against the same band. §6 couples through whichever model passes. Where neither passes, §6 uses the measured H(f) of the measured pairs and M/L for the rest.

nova's structure at nominal resistivity, with nothing fitted, predicts eight of the nine pairs within the band, at 4–8 % of M/L. EF1→EF6 misses at 18.8 %. Realigning E100353's channels changes nothing, so the miss is not a timing artefact. The reverse pair, EF6→EF1, passes at 6.5 %, as do EF1→EF2 from the same shot and EF5→EF6 with EF6 as the pickup. The miss is therefore particular to EF1 driving EF6. On 2026-10-13 the lead chose to test EF6's loading before closing §5: whether EF6 carried current during that test, so that it was a loaded rather than an open pickup, and whether a loaded-pickup model brings EF1→EF6 within the band while the passing pairs stay within it. Records: jccm-nova-modes, jccm-ef1-ef6.

EF6 was an open pickup. During E100353 it carried under 1 A of induced current, against 175 A when EF6 itself was driven, and both of its supply references were zero. A fitted series load leaves EF1→EF6 at 18.6 % and needs 7 H, ten times EF6's own inductance (jccm-ef6-loading). On 2026-10-13 the lead closed §5 on nova's passive structure at nominal resistivity, which meets the band on eight of nine pairs. Two items stay open, with their evidence: EF1→EF6 at 18.8 %, whose cause is not timing and not pickup loading, and the EF5→EF4 excess at 12f, which no inductive model here reproduces. §6 couples through nova below 30 Hz, and through the measured H(f) for EF1→EF6 alone.

Done when a passive model, either free loops or nova's geometry with fitted resistivity scales, fitted through the coupled circuit equations on a training set of pairs, predicts the H(f) of each held-out pair over 0.1–30 Hz within 10 % rms of its M/L. A model that misses the band does not meet this done-when; its miss is recorded as measured. If both models miss, §5 closes only by a decision of the lead recorded in this plan, never by this done-when. Negative control: the same held-out pairs predicted by M/L alone, without the modes, miss by more than that. The complex ratios at 6f, 12f and 18f are recorded for every coil pair the data reach, from the single-coil tests and the fast discharges, with their spread over repeat shots. They are the couplings §6 uses at those frequencies, whether or not a shared extension of the mode model also describes them; pairs the data do not reach are listed. The time constants of nova's own passive-structure model, from pf_passive, are reported beside the identified ones.

§6 — The coil ripple lines with the converter sources

Add the converter sources to §7's assembly: the booster bridges and the EF2–EF5 base supplies from booster-converter-model, and the CS1–4, EF1 and EF6 base supplies configured from the topology jt60sa-power-supply-sources §7 cites. At 6f, 12f and 18f the coils are coupled through §5's measured complex ratios, with §3's channel signs applied. Predict the coil voltages of a 2023 shot that runs every supply (E101088 or E101089), including the ripple each coil picks up from the others.

The supplies enter through the supply model's own chain, so each stage is applied once, by its owner: SupplyModel.source_phasors gives the converter coefficients before the loop, coil_phasors applies the booster loop (filter_network.py), and acquired_phasors applies the acquisition chain. This section waits on gate g-jccm-1: until booster-converter-model §5 passes, a line the run misses cannot be told from a supply-model miss. The lead split the slow coil currents out into §7 on 2026-10-14, so that half runs while §5 stays open.

Done when the predicted coil-voltage lines from 6f to 18f on all ten coils lie within the tolerance the lead set for the S1 prediction (filter-grounding-prediction §1: 3 dB, or 5 V where the measured line is below 10 V) for every coil whose couplings §5 reaches. Negative control: the same run, with the same sources and windows, but with §5's line couplings set to zero, misses the band on a coil and line that §5's catalogue reaches and that is named in this plan before the run. That shows the coupling terms carry the pickup.

§7 — The slow coil currents of the coupled system

Drive every coil circuit with its own measured terminal voltage below 30 Hz (MMSYS/vol<coil>, low-passed, with §3's channel signs) and solve the voltage-driven state equations of the ten active coils and nova's passive structure together, at nominal resistivity (power_convertor.passive_structure), with the coil and passive inductances of the machine description §4 wrote. The predicted coil currents are compared with the measured MMSYS/cur<coil>LKAT; no measured coil current is prescribed. This half needs no converter model. A coil's terminal voltage is its supplies' output as applied, so the run tests the coupled inductance and the passive structure on their own, apart from the supply model, whose held-out check (booster-converter-model §5) has not passed. EF1→EF6 is judged on nova's coupling, the model §5 closed on; the same run with EF1→EF6 set to its measured slow ratio is reported beside it and not judged.

The judgement is made over short windows, not over whole shots. Integrating a terminal voltage over a 50 s shot and asking for the current within 5 % needs the voltage right to about a volt, while the channels carry offsets of 20–40 V that shift by up to 28 V once the supplies energise (s7-offset). Whole-shot integration therefore measures channel stability, not the coupling. Over a 1–2 s window a volt of offset moves a coil current by a few amperes, so a window tests the coupling. The judged windows are of two kinds. The first is the 1–2 s current ramps of the plasma-free kind-E shots E101001 and E101005, where some coil's current changes by at least 500 A. The second is the single-coil CS fast discharges held from §2, where one module dumps alone and the CS currents differ, which the kind-E ramps do not give. Each window begins after at least 0.5 s with every coil current flat, so the passive currents have decayed. It starts from the measured coil currents and zero filament current. Each voltage's reference is its mean over a flat span in the same supply state as the window, because the channel level moves when a supply energises. A kind-E window lies wholly inside the energised interval, and its reference is an energised flat span. In a fast discharge the dumping module's supply is bypassed from the dump onward, so that module's reference is its supplies-off level on the same shot, and every other coil keeps its energised reference. A window whose shot carries no reference span in the right state is reported, not judged. Nothing is fitted to a judged window. The whole-shot integration is still reported, and not judged. The new surface is the assembly, which replaces nothing because no existing module drives several coils at once, and §6 extends it with the converter sources. nova's propagator integrates passive modes from a supplied flux history and cannot predict the coil currents, so it serves only to cross-check the passive response to the predicted currents.

Done when each coil's predicted current change over a judged window follows its measured change within 5 % of the largest coil-current change in that window. That holds in at least 90 % of the judged windows and is beyond 10 % in none, for every coil, run on the all_debug partition. Negative control: the same windows with the coil-to-coil mutual inductances and the coil–passive coupling set to zero miss that band on CS2 in a CS1 or CS3 fast discharge, named here before the run. In those windows CS2's own change is small, and its terminal voltage carries the dumping neighbour's mutual EMF.

§8 — Why EF1 driving EF6 misses nova's passive structure

§5 closed on nova's passive structure with one miss recorded. The EF1→EF6 terminal ratio from E100353 sits 18.8 % of M/L from nova's prediction over 0.1–30 Hz. The reverse pair, EF6→EF1 (E100351), sits at 6.5 %, EF1→EF2 at 7.7 %, and the other six pairs at 3.9–7.3 %. Timing and EF6 loading are ruled out (s5-ef1-ef6, s5-ef6-loading). The EF1 dump E100352 gives EF6's slow coupling at 94.4 % of nova's. This section asks whether the miss comes from the coil geometry in the machine description or from a passive conductor that nova's 155 filaments (98 vessel, 57 cryostat) do not carry.

The two leave different signatures. A geometry error in EF1 or EF6 (radius, height, cross-section, turns, or the sign of their mutual) scales the coupling by a fixed factor at every frequency, the slow limit included. A missing conductor screens the field only below its own decay rate, so it changes H(f) over a band and leaves the slow limit as nova has it. Neither fits the measured pattern unaided. The screened mutual is the same in both directions, so a conductor can make the two directions differ only through the driving coil's own screening, in the ratio's denominator. EF1→EF2 shares that denominator with EF1→EF6, yet sits inside the band. A miss confined to EF1→EF6 therefore needs a conductor on the flux path between EF1 and EF6 whose effect EF6→EF1 does not show, a geometry error, or a condition particular to the EF1-driven shots. The spread across EF1-driven shots points at the third: the 2023 shots E100839, E100909 and E100859 give 16.3 %, 14.0 % and 7.8 %.

Five measurements settle it. The first is more EF1-driven data. The run fetches the further 2021 and 2023 single-coil EF1 booster tests and EF1 fast discharges that the EDDB catalogue holds, with EF6 and EF2 recorded, into the main checkout's data/jt60sa/ef1_coupling. On each it measures H(f) for EF1→EF6 and EF1→EF2 and the slow ratio, through transfer_scoring and §7's slow-part estimator. The second is the geometry. EF1's and EF6's radius, height, cross-section and turns in the machine description §4 wrote are compared with the cited JT-60SA coil data, and EF1's self-inductance with its fast discharges. The third is the candidate conductors. Every toroidally continuous conductor near EF1 or EF6 that nova's model lacks is listed from the JT-60SA design documents and the imas-ambix machine description, with its location, cross-section and resistivity. Candidates include the cryostat top lid and base, the TF coil casings where the outer intercoil structure closes them toroidally, the thermal shields, and the EF coil supports. Each is added to nova's structure as documented, with nothing fitted, and the nine measured pairs are re-scored. The fourth is the shot conditions. For every EF1-driven shot held, the run records which other supplies were energised or in circuit, and each coil's current and reference. It then sets the EF1→EF6 error against them, to test whether the miss follows a shot condition rather than the hardware.

The fifth is the dump waveforms. A fast discharge is a single transient, and the cross-spectral estimate keeps only two or three coherent bins on one (s8-dumps), so the dumps are read in the time domain instead. On each 2023 EF1 fast discharge (E100904, E100905, E101055 and E101056), EF1's measured terminal voltage over the dump window drives nova's nominal structure, and the run predicts the voltage EF6 and EF2 pick up. This is the time-domain form of the terminal ratio. It is computed through §7's coupled solve, or by applying terminal_ratio to the spectrum of EF1's voltage and transforming back, rather than with new physics. Each prediction is scored against the measured pickup: the rms of the difference over the window, as a percentage of the measured pickup's peak. Every voltage channel is first referenced by §7's supply-state rule. The dumped coil takes its settled level after the dump, once its supply is bypassed. Each pickup coil takes its own level over a flat span before the dump, in its own state (s7-offset). The supplies-off levels reach +34.6 V on EF1, +33.4 V on EF5 and −10.3 V on EF6. Those are comparable to the weak pickups, so an unreferenced offset would be scored as coupling. The same is done on the 2023 EF6 and EF5 fast discharges E101079, E101081, E101116 and E101117, fetched one at a time into the main checkout's data/jt60sa/fast_discharge. Those give EF6→EF1, the reverse pair, and EF6→EF5, EF6→EF4, EF5→EF4 and EF5→EF6, which §5 found inside the band. A pair fits when its score is within 10 %. The EF5- and EF6-driven pairs are the positive control: if they do not fit, the waveform test is not validated, and the run judges nothing about EF1 from it. If they fit, the two outcomes separate. If EF1→EF6 misses while EF1→EF2 fits, the offset is real and particular to EF1 driving EF6. If both EF1 pairs fit, the miss on E100353 belongs to the booster tests rather than the hardware.

Done when the run names the cause the numbers support (a geometry error, a missing conductor, or neither) and records: EF1→EF6's slow ratio and H(f) on every EF1-driven shot held, each geometry quantity against its cited value, for each candidate conductor the leave-one-pair-out rms of all nine pairs, the EF1→EF6 error against each shot condition, and the waveform score of every pair on every dump the fifth measurement names, in both arms. A candidate is accepted only if, at its documented geometry and resistivity, it brings EF1→EF6 inside the 10 % band and keeps the other eight pairs inside it. The run is on the all_debug partition. Negative controls: re-scoring with nova's structure unchanged must reproduce EF1→EF6 at 18.8 %. The acceptance check must also reject a synthetic candidate that changes only EF1's own screening, because that moves EF1→EF2 by the same proportion as EF1→EF6. In the waveform test, the arm with the passive structure removed must score worse than nova's structure on every dump. If it does not, the dumps are too slow to show the screening, and the run says so rather than reading the scores as a fit.

§9 — nova's coil coupling at the converter harmonics

This section measures how well nova's coupled network of coils and passive structure carries converter ripple from one coil to another. That is the uncertainty the ITER model needs. ITER's current supplies put their lines in the same band as JT-60SA's (ITER coil supply topology):

  • twelve-pulse thyristor PF units on a 50 Hz grid, at 600 Hz and 1200 Hz;
  • six-pulse VS units, at 300 Hz;
  • the Stage 2 IGBT units, at 500 Hz and 1600 Hz.

ITER has no measured coil coupling at any of those frequencies. JT-60SA's 6f, 12f and 18f lines sit at about 365, 730 and 1095 Hz on a supply near 61 Hz.

No converter source model enters, because both terminals of every pair are measured. The pickup coil's terminal load is a passive part of the network and is modelled as one: its idle supply, and in 2023 the ripple filter at its design values. The lead set this scope on 2026-10-15. It replaces §6's whole-shot prediction on this plan's path, since that prediction tests JT-60SA's own converter models, which do not carry to ITER's different converters.

The measurement is §5's record of measured complex line ratios (s5-lines): 52 ratios at 6f, 12f and 18f across 29 year-pairs, from the 2021 and 2023 single-coil booster tests, each with its spread over repeat shots. They are regenerated with scripts/jt60sa/harmonic_coupling_scan.py and read with §3's channel signs applied.

The prediction comes from the coupled plant that nova's coupled_plant call returns, the same plant the switched replay and the ITER work take. The run reads it through NovaPlantModel.terminal_ratio in scripts/jt60sa/op2_plant.py at each line's own measured frequency, at nominal resistivity, with nothing fitted, and compares it with M/L alone. harmonic_transfers in that script already sets the plant's |H| beside the measured line for part of the pair set, with a no-passive control. The run extends that function to every line §5 recorded, to the phase, and to the score below, rather than writing a second scorer.

Which prediction is scored:

  • 2021: the open-pickup ratio, with the idle supply taken as open.
  • 2023: the ratio with the ripple filter across the pickup terminals wherever filter_network places one. It is computed from the plant's terminal impedance with BoosterFilter.shunt_impedance as the load. loaded_pickup's terminal ratio is extended from its scalar series load to a complex load impedance to do this, rather than a new helper being added.

The 2023 lines are also reported open, so the filter's effect on each ratio is visible. A 2023 pickup that the run cannot place a filter on is scored open and listed.

Each line is scored by its amplitude error, |Hnova| / |Hmeas| − 1 in %, and its phase error in degrees. A line fits when the amplitude error is within 10 % and the phase error within 10°, or within twice the line's repeat spread where that is larger. For each harmonic the run reports the median and the largest error of both arms. The result is stated as a band per harmonic that the ITER model can carry. Three kinds of line are reported apart rather than averaged into the band:

  • Opposite sides of M/L: lines where nova and the measurement sit on opposite sides of M/L. There the network's screening moves the ratio the wrong way, which points at a path the inductive network does not carry, such as a capacitive or grounding path, rather than at a wrong resistivity. EF5→EF4 at 12f is the known case: measured 0.568, M/L 0.288, nova 0.065.
  • Moved between years: pairs measured in both years whose ratio moves between them. 2023 carries the filter and the alternative grounding, so such a move separates what the loading explains from what it does not.
  • Skin depth: each harmonic's skin depth in the vessel and cryostat walls, set against the wall thickness the machine description gives. One filament across a wall holds only while the skin depth exceeds the thickness.

Done when:

  • A JSON under the main checkout's data/jt60sa/harmonic_nova/ lists every line with its frequency, measured ratio and spread, the nova and M/L ratios with both errors, the assumed loading, and the per-harmonic bands.
  • A fragment states the bands, the fit count per harmonic, the opposite-side and year-moved lines, and the skin-depth table.
  • One SVG under docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/harmonic-nova plots measured against predicted amplitude and phase for each harmonic.
  • A unit test pins one line's nova ratio.

Positive control: before anything is scored, the run reproduces §5's recorded measured ratios from the traces within their stated precision. Negative control: scaling the vessel and cryostat resistivity must move the pinned test's ratio outside its tolerance. If nova and M/L agree within the band on every line, the run says the passive structure is not exercised at these frequencies, and the section reports that instead of a band. The work is computational and runs in place on the fleet allocation.

§10 — Wall resolution at the converter harmonics

§9 found nova over-screening every measured harmonic line, by a median 80–93 %, with a single filament across each wall where the skin depth is thinner than the wall. Nova can now divide walls through their thickness. The ITER coordinator's passive-skin-effect node added this (nova 207a66408), and the lead asked for it to be validated on these lines.

The option is set on the machine. passive_thickness_m gives each passive circuit's plate thickness, and passive_layer_count gives the interior strips. Each face also carries a strip thinner than a seventh of the skin depth at 5 kHz. One layer reproduces the existing plant, so studies that do not set the option are unchanged. The lead requires that this stays so: layered walls are for fast-transient and ripple studies only.

On ITER, two and four layers agree to four decimals. Against the one-layer plant they lower coil-to-coil transfer by up to about 5 % at 300–1600 Hz, which is more screening. The physical reason is that a resolved wall excludes flux at its face rather than at its mid-plane, so resolution should widen JT-60SA's gap rather than close it. This section measures whether it does.

Three measurements:

  • Plate thickness. The OP2 description's filament widths (vessel 20–60 mm, cryostat 34–80 mm) may be envelopes that lump the vessel's double wall and ribs into one filament, which would understate the skin effect. The run takes each circuit's conducting plate thickness from the vessel and cryostat documents under data/sources/, or from the machine description where it states plates, and names the source. Where no document gives a plate thickness, it scores both the envelope and the documented plate as bounds.
  • Re-score. The JT-60SA plant is built through op2_plant with two layers and with four, and the 52 lines are re-scored by §9's rule. Per line, the run reports the change against the one-layer plant. The three lines that sit on the opposite side of M/L are reported apart: EF5→EF4 12f, EF5→CS4 12f and 2023 EF2→CS1 6f.
  • Surface impedance compared. The lead asked whether a frequency-dependent skin effect is a better model than a resolved mesh. The run compares two models against the closed-form shell solution, the same check nova's node passed: the strips, and a frequency-dependent surface impedance Zs = (1 + j)ρ/δ per unit area on the existing one-filament walls. A thin shell carrying that impedance is the same model. Both are also scored on the 52 lines. The surface impedance grows as √f, so it needs a rational fit before a time-domain model can use it, and the strips do not. The fragment states that trade beside the accuracy.

Done when:

  • A JSON under the main checkout's data/jt60sa/harmonic_layers/ carries every line's ratio under one layer, two layers, four layers and the surface impedance, with the thickness used and its source for each passive circuit.
  • A fragment, jccm-harmonic-layers, states the per-harmonic bands for each model, the change against one layer, the three opposite-side lines, and the shell check of both models.
  • One SVG under docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/harmonic-layers plots it.
  • A unit test pins one line's two-layer ratio.

Positive control: at nova's current main, §9's pinned one-layer EF5→EF4 12f ratio, 0.06469, is reproduced unchanged before any layer is added. Negative control: the surface-impedance arm with ρ scaled a hundredfold must move the pinned shell check outside its tolerance. If layering moves no line by more than its repeat spread, the run says wall resolution is not the cause at these frequencies.

The work is computational and runs in place on the fleet allocation. It changes nothing in nova: the surface impedance enters through power_convertor's own terminal-ratio path.

§11 — The circuit at the pickup terminals, 2021 and 2023

§9 scored nova with the pickup open in 2021 and the filter's design shunt across the pickup terminals in 2023. The installed shunt sits across the booster branch, not the terminals, so the 2023 arm modelled a circuit the machine does not have. The measured ratios also moved between years: by ×0.24 to ×4.5 on fourteen pairs, and by ×89 on EF2→CS1 6f. Three lines sit on the far side of M/L, where an inductive network cannot follow.

This section models what actually sits across each pickup coil's terminals at the harmonics, in each year, and tests whether that circuit explains the year moves and the opposite-side lines. Five elements:

  • the idle supply's state, from the converter documents and the shot's own supply references: open, bypass or circulating current;
  • the 2023 booster-branch filter at its installed attachment, filter_network.BoosterLoop with shunt_attachment="booster_only". The model's default, "as_drawn", puts the shunt across both supplies, which the machine does not have;
  • the coil's own capacitance and its cable to ground, bounded by what the switched replay measured. booster-converter-model §14 fitted a resonance near 936 Hz, and no documented component supplies it. jt60sa-switched-pulse-replay §3 measured the available capacitance at 2.87–5.92 µF, against the 6.44–14.63 µF a 730–1100 Hz resonance needs, and found no resonance. The documented 0.6 µF screen with the 3.25 mH booster loop resonates near 3.6 kHz. So the run carries a terminal resonance only as a candidate inside that measured range, never as a fitted one;
  • the 2023 alternative grounding;
  • whether the voltage channel measures the coil differentially or each terminal to ground, from the measurement documents. If the channel reads each terminal to ground, a common-mode path can carry the driven coil's voltage into the pickup's channel.

Each element enters through the repository model that already represents it, not through a routing chosen here. A single element can act in two ways:

  • Across the coil terminals, closing the pickup coil's own loop. The grounding's differential resistance, about 4 kΩ, works this way, as do the capacitance across the terminals and the cable's inter-bar capacitance.
  • From each terminal to ground, carrying a common-mode voltage.

filter_network.BoosterLoop and GroundingSystem already carry both parts: the shunt across the coil terminals, and common_mode and terminal_to_ground. busbar_lines carries the cable's inter-bar and to-ground capacitance. The loop-closing parts reach nova's open-pickup prediction as loaded_pickup's complex load. The common-mode parts reach the channel by its measurement mode: a channel that reads each terminal to ground sees the driven coil's common-mode voltage.

For each element the run states which part closes the loop and which is common-mode, with the model that supplies each, and reports its effect on every line.

An element whose values no document gives is scored across a stated range rather than fitted. Scoring follows §12: the lines §12 classed coupled, and the mixed lines' differential ratios. Each line's class is shown beside its result, and the 18 unresolved lines are reported separately.

Done when:

  • A JSON under the main checkout's data/jt60sa/pickup_circuit/ carries each element, its source and values, and every line's ratio with and without it.
  • A fragment, jccm-pickup-circuit, states which elements move which lines and whether any combination brings the year moves and the opposite-side lines within §9's rule.
  • One SVG under docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/pickup-circuit plots it.
  • A unit test pins one loaded ratio against an independently computed circuit value, which also answers §9's review follow-on.

Negative control: with every element removed, the run reproduces §9's open-pickup ratios exactly. A line no element moves is reported as unexplained, not fitted. The work is computational and runs in place on the fleet allocation.

§12 — Whether the pickup line is the pickup's own

§9's measured ratios assume that the line on the pickup coil at 6f, 12f or 18f is the driven coil's line coupled across. That holds only if the pickup's own supply makes no line at the same frequency. booster-converter-model §18 and §21 found that a base supply at zero voltage reference carries 91–111 V of 12f on its coil, and §5 accepted lines only where the pickup's supply reference sat within ±5 V. Every converter runs from the same motor-generator, so a line the pickup's own supply makes sits at the same frequency as the coupled one, and the ratio estimator cannot separate them.

A self-made line would explain three things §9 found:

  • measured ratios above nova, and some above M/L;
  • ratios that move between 2021 and 2023, as the 2023 filter changed each supply's ripple;
  • the largest misses at 12f, the twelve-pulse base's own line.

The lead set this test to run before §10 and §11 on 2026-10-16, because it decides whether §9's ratios measure coupling at all.

For each of the 52 lines, from the traces §5 used, the run measures three things:

  • The pickup's line without the driver. In spans of the same shot where the driven booster does not carry the line and the pickup's supply reference holds the same ±5 V state, the run measures the pickup coil's line at the same harmonic, locked to the shot's own fundamental, and reports its amplitude against the line §5 recorded.
  • Scaling with the driver. Across the repeat shots of each pair, the run tests whether the pickup line's amplitude follows the driven line's and whether its phase relative to the driven line holds. A coupled line does both; a self-made one does neither.
  • The pickup supply's state. Whether the pickup's base supply was firing or blocked in the window, read from its reference and DC channels (PSSCfst/refvol<coil>Bse, <coil>/volPSDC) or the shot records.

Each line is classed as coupled, self-made or mixed, with its evidence. Where a mixed line's own part has a stable phase, the run subtracts it coherently and re-scores the corrected ratio against nova by §9's rule. A line whose own part cannot be measured is listed, not corrected.

Done when:

  • A JSON under the main checkout's data/jt60sa/own_line/ carries every line's class, its line without the driver, the scaling and phase evidence, the supply state and any corrected ratio.
  • A fragment, jccm-own-line, states the class counts per harmonic, the corrected nova band where one exists, and what the result means for §9's verdict.
  • One SVG under docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/own-line plots it.
  • A unit test pins one line's split.

Positive control: a synthetic pickup trace is built from a driven line through a known ratio plus a self-made line at the same frequency with a different phase. The run must split it into its two parts within 5 %. Negative control: a synthetic, purely coupled line must be classed coupled, with no own part.

The work is computational and runs in place on the fleet allocation, with no change to nova.

§13 — An upper bound on 3D eddy paths

Three candidates are now ruled out as the cause of nova's harmonic over-screening:

  • contamination by the pickup's own supply (§12);
  • the documented pickup-terminal circuit (§11);
  • wall resolution, which on ITER adds screening rather than removing it.

One candidate the axisymmetric model cannot represent remains: ports and breaks that interrupt the toroidal eddy currents a continuous wall would carry. The lead chose to bound it on 2026-10-16.

Treating a port as added resistance cannot matter at these frequencies. The walls' modes are deep in the inductive limit, and §9's hundredfold resistivity mutation moved EF5→EF4 12f only from 0.065 to 0.083. The bound is therefore a cut: a wall's toroidal current path removed outright. That is the most a port can do, because a real port interrupts only part of the circumference.

Two measurements:

  • Which conductors screen each line. The OP2 export carries two passive loops, VV and CRYOSTAT, with one label each. The run therefore defines groups by filament position (r, z) within those loops: the vessel's inboard, outboard, upper and lower walls, and the cryostat's body, base and lid. It records each group's boundary and filament count. For each group, the run removes that group and re-scores the lines §12 classed coupled, and the mixed lines' differential ratios. It reports per line which group carries its screening.
  • The port bound. The run takes the poloidal positions of the vessel and cryostat ports from the machine description or the vessel documents, and names the source. It removes the passive filaments at those positions, all together, and re-scores the same lines.

For each line the run reports nova's cut ratio beside the measured ratio and M/L. The reading:

  • If the full port cut still leaves nova below the measured coupling, 3D eddy paths are ruled out as the cause.
  • If the cut reaches or passes the measured coupling, ports can explain it within the bound. The real, partial effect then needs a 3D model, and the section says which lines and which ports.

The cuts are made on the passive circuits passed to nova's coupled plant, through op2_plant, with no change to nova. Scoring goes through op2_plant.harmonic_transfers. The node also replaces the copy of that scoring in scripts/jt60sa/pickup_terminal_circuit.py with a call to it, as §11's review asked, so one acceptance rule serves every harmonic section.

Done when:

  • A JSON under the main checkout's data/jt60sa/passive_cuts/ carries every cut, its filaments and source, and every scored line's ratio under each cut.
  • A fragment, jccm-passive-cuts, states the screening group per line, the port-bound reading, and what it means for ITER's axisymmetric walls.
  • One SVG under docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/passive-cuts plots it.
  • A unit test pins one cut ratio.

Positive control: with no cut, the run reproduces §9's nominal ratios exactly. Negative control: removing every passive filament reproduces §9's no-passive arm.

The work is computational and runs in place on the fleet allocation.

§14 — Whether the harmonic coupling is magnetic

Nova fits the measured coil-to-coil transfer functions from 0.1 to 30 Hz (§5), but sits 80–93 % low on the 365–1100 Hz converter lines (§9). Four explanations are ruled out:

  • contamination by the pickup's own supply (§12);
  • the documented pickup-terminal circuit (§11);
  • wall resolution, which on ITER adds screening;
  • ports, where the strongest cut lifts no line to its measurement (§13).

The stored transfer functions suggest why none of these worked. Nine pairs have both a measured transfer function from §5 and harmonic lines. For those nine, each line sits 0.4 to 9 times above the measured coupling at the sample nearest 25 Hz. Four pairs reach 3× on at least one line, EF5→EF4 the most, at 9× on 6f and 7.6× on 12f. Nova's coupling falls or stays flat over that band, as it must, because eddy currents in the walls screen more as frequency rises. A coupling that rises with frequency is therefore not magnetic. This section tests that reading on every pair, using data already held. It runs before the harmonic work closes, as the lead decided on 2026-10-17.

Of the twenty pairs the harmonic work scores, nine have a measured transfer function from §5. Only those nine can be joined across the band, so every class count states this denominator. The other eleven are reported apart: where a pair has lines at more than one harmonic, the trend from 6f to 12f to 18f is given against nova's over the same lines, and a pair with a single line is listed unclassed.

For each of the nine pairs, the run joins §5's measured transfer function (0.1–30 Hz, from the booster tests) to its harmonic lines: the lines §12 classed coupled, and the mixed lines' differential ratios. It computes nova's and M/L's coupling on the same frequency grid through op2_plant, and states which shots each part comes from. Each pair is classed:

  • Magnetic: the measured coupling follows nova's trend above 30 Hz, so the harmonic gap is a level offset.
  • Rising: the measured coupling rises with frequency while nova's falls, so the harmonic excess is non-magnetic.

For a rising pair the run reports the excess, the measured coupling minus nova's, as a complex ratio: its slope in log |H| against log f, and its phase relative to the driven line. The lead has confirmed that ITER's coils carry grounding paint on their ground insulation, which makes their capacitance coil-to-ground rather than coil-to-coil. The run first finds, from the documents, whether JT-60SA's EF coils carry the same paint. If they do, coil-to-coil capacitance is set aside and two routes remain. If they do not, or the documents do not say, coil-to-coil capacitance stays as a third route. It has the same growing-with-f, +90° signature as capacitance to ground and cannot be told from it by slope and phase alone, so the run reports such a pair as capacitive without naming which capacitance. The routes' signatures:

  • Capacitance to ground with common mode through the grounding gives an excess growing about as f, with a phase lead near +90°.
  • A voltage tap that reads a terminal to ground gives an excess set by the grounding divider, roughly flat in frequency.

The run states which signature each rising pair's excess fits, or that it fits neither. It does not force a route.

Done when:

  • A JSON under the main checkout's data/jt60sa/frequency_trend/ carries per pair the joined measured curve with its shots, nova's and M/L's curves, the class, and for rising pairs the excess's slope and phase with the route it fits.
  • A fragment, jccm-frequency-trend, gives the class counts, the routes, and the reading for ITER.
  • One SVG under docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/frequency-trend plots |H| and phase against frequency for each pair, measured, nova and M/L.
  • A unit test pins one pair's excess slope.

Positive control: a synthetic pair built from nova's own coupling must class magnetic. The same pair with an added excess growing as f with a +90° lead must class rising, with slope 1 ± 0.1 and the capacitive signature. Negative control: nova's curve must reproduce §5's fit from 0.1 to 30 Hz and §9's values on the lines before any pair is classed.

The work is computational, uses only held data, makes no change to nova, and runs in place on the fleet allocation.

§15 — The 2023 pulses, with the filter, the new grounding and the plasma

Moved here on 17 October 2026 from jt60sa-switched-pulse-replay §6, by the lead's decision in the portfolio review, so that one plan carries the JT-60SA coupling question to its end. The 2023 restart added a ripple filter and a new grounding with design values, which is a controlled change in the stray network. The plasma pulses need a shot-matched equilibrium. None is held. It is asked for from the site (EQDB, a g-file or an IMAS equilibrium) in one bounded query, and nova takes it as a reconstructed plasma source (iter-passive-plasma-circuit §5). The section is held by gate g-jccm-4 on that source, and it reads §14's verdict on whether the harmonic coupling is magnetic before it scores anything.

Done when the strays bounded from 2021, unchanged, predict the 2023 lines through the filter and the new grounding. Score them as jt60sa-switched-pulse-replay §5 scored the 2021 windows. Negative control: putting the 2021 grounding in place of the 2023 one moves the predicted lines by the amount the design change implies.

§16 — Whether the windings' distributed capacitance explains the rising coupling

§14 found that six of the nine joinable pairs couple more strongly with frequency from 20 Hz through the converter lines while nova stays flat. The excess grows as f0.25–0.62 with a lag of 11–29°. Lumped capacitance, to ground or between coils, would grow as f with a 90° lead. §11's lumped coil and cable capacitance, within its 5.92 µF bound, fits no joint set of the 27 lines.

The one capacitive form not yet scored is the capacitance distributed through each winding. Below a damped winding mode the terminal coupling rises with a growing lag, which is the shape measured. JT-60SA's lines, at about 365, 730 and 1,095 Hz, sit just below its ideal winding modes (868 Hz–2.43 kHz). The 2021 replay also needed more capacitance at 730–1,100 Hz than the stray estimates gave. The lead asked on 17 October 2026 for this test, because the EF windings are built like ITER's PF windings and the answer transfers.

Score the six rising pairs, with the three that follow nova as controls, through the coupled plant with distributed windings from shared-coil-supply-model §3. There are two kinds of free parameter. The first is one insulation scale for each coil family (EF single pancakes, EF double pancakes, CS). It is applied to every turn, section and ground capacitance of that family, within the range in the replay windings record. The second is the installed damping, as a stated interval, as on ITER. Fit on half the rising pairs and predict the other half, then swap. Predict the three magnetic pairs as well; they must stay flat.

Done when the derived JT-60SA plant caches this section consumes have been rerun on the regenerated thick-coil matrices (b89fdb0f), with every score that moves tabulated against its earlier recorded value, and the record states, for each pair, the measured and predicted slope and phase from 20 Hz through the lines, and the 6f, 12f and 18f line ratios against §9's rule, all under that cross-validation. It also states which of three verdicts holds:

  • the distributed winding explains the rising excess: both held-out halves are within §9's rule on at least two thirds of their scoreable lines, with slopes within 0.1;
  • it explains part of it;
  • it does not, and any fitted scale that sits at a range end is named.

The verdict and the fitted scales go to the ITER coordinator as a transferable result: either the insulation scale ITER's windings should carry, or the statement that ITER's harmonic coupling stays empirical.

Positive control: a synthetic pair generated with a known insulation scale is recovered within 5 %. Negative control: with zero capacitance, the predicted slopes reproduce nova's flat −0.01 to 0.03. The pairs are scored through the plant §9, §13 and §14 use, scripts/jt60sa/op2_plant.py's NovaPlantModel.terminal_ratio and harmonic_transfers, extended to carry shared-coil-supply-model §3's section-resolved winding ports. No second scorer is added, and the earlier scripts/jt60sa/sectioned_plant.py build is not used. The caller is scripts/jt60sa/winding_coupling_score.py with its test tests/test_winding_coupling_score.py. Rows and logs go to data/jt60sa/winding_coupling/, the figure to docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/winding-coupling, and the record to the fragment docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/winding-coupling.html.

§17 — The 2023 coil-only pulses through the filter and the new grounding

§15's question, whether the strays bounded on 2021 predict the 2023 converter lines through the new ripple filter and grounding, does not need a plasma. Two facts settle this. The 2023 shot census (fragment shot-census-2023, merged at 828f7255) found that 28 of the 29 held 2023 shots carry no plasma and fire a booster with a measurable 6f line (37–375 V, SNR 11–153). Eighteen of them are single-converter coil tests on EF1, EF2, EF5 and EF6: E100676, E100678, E100839, E100859, E100908, E100909 (EF1); E100863, E100864, E100915, E100917 (EF2); E100865, E100866, E100921, E100922 (EF5); E100882, E100883, E100927, E100928 (EF6). These are the direct 2023 counterparts of the 2021 booster tests. The SELENE check (merged at 5cef5365) found that in the coupled plant a prescribed plasma contributes nothing to coil-to-coil coupling at 6f, 12f and 18f, by construction. So the coil-only pulses carry the whole test as the model stands. §15 keeps the plasma pulses, behind gate g-jccm-4.

Score the eighteen single-converter tests as §9, §13 and §14 scored the 2021 lines: a coil-to-coil terminal ratio, taken here through the composed JT-60SA plant rather than the bare one. The owner is power_convertor.jt60sa_circuits: composed_plant() over the coupled plant, and ComposedPlantModel.terminal_ratio(frequency_hz, driven, pickup). It composes each coil's circuit from the register (registers/jt60sa_supplies.json), with the as-built alternative grounding: the 2 kΩ and 45 kΩ pairs of jt60sa-power-supply-sources §3. It does not yet install the ripple filter. build_circuit reads the register's filter key but composes only the supply, series unit, coil, line and grounding. So before §17 can score, that owner must install the 2023 filter on every booster coil from the register, with the shunt across the booster branch as §11 corrected. §18 does that. Each shot's measured driven-coil lines, in the census's line window, are the input. The predicted lines on each pickup, and their ratio to the driven coil against §9's rule, are the score. No converter model is needed, so shots on all four boosters can be scored. Use the 2021-bounded strays unchanged. No parameter is refit on 2023. Each shot's campaign comes from the census's catalogue dates, not from the shot number.

Never build the scored circuit from filter_network.BoosterLoop's as_drawn default, which puts the shunt across both supplies, a circuit the machine does not have. Never build it from scripts/jt60sa/replay_2021.py's replay_pulse either: that replay carries neither the 2023 filter nor the alternative grounding; its receivers carry only a stated 1 kΩ grounding shunt. A test asserts the filter attachment and the grounding the scored circuit carries. The two variants the controls and the EF6 arm need are register variants built through the same owner, never a second builder: the 2021 circuit (no filter, the 2021 grounding) and the 2023 circuit with EF6's filter removed. The 2021 grounding has no sourced value in this repository: filter-grounding-prediction describes it only as single-ended, before the alternative system. Its terminal-to-ground resistances must be sourced from the JT-60SA documents before the year move or the negative control can be computed. §19 does that. §17 waits on §18 and §19.

The six multi-booster pulses (E100963, E100964, E101087–E101090) are listed and not scored. §9's rule is a ratio between one driven coil and one pickup, and a pulse with two or more boosters firing together has no single driven coil. The census itself advises preferring the single-converter tests.

EF6's filter state in 2023 is not established. jt60sa-power-supply-sources §3 lists the per-filter installation dates as open, and EF6's 2023 ripple behaves as if the trap were absent. The census repeats that caveat. So the four EF6 shots (E100882, E100883, E100927, E100928) form their own arm, scored twice: once with the filter at its design values and once with no filter. They are left out of the claim's verdict. Their record states which filter state the lines favour and by how much, against §9's rule. That state is a finding for the source register, not a fitted parameter. A miss on EF1, EF2 or EF5 may be attributed to the filter, because the collective statement that the modifications preceded the August 2023 restart covers them.

The caller is scripts/jt60sa/coil_only_2023.py with its test tests/test_coil_only_2023.py. Rows and logs go to the main checkout's /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/power_convertor/data/jt60sa/coil_only_2023/, never a worktree-relative data/, the figure to docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/coil-only-2023, and the record to the fragment docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/coil-only-2023.html.

Before scoring anything, the node reads §14's verdict on whether the harmonic coupling is magnetic, as §15 must. The absolute ratios inherit the plant's known error: on 2021 data, which carries neither the 2023 filter nor the 2023 grounding, §9 found the same plant over-screening these lines by a median 80–93 %. The absolute 2023 ratios are recorded, but they are expected to reproduce that over-screening, and they decide nothing about the filter or the grounding. The claim is judged on the year move instead. For each pair and line, take the change in the coil-to-coil ratio from a matching 2021 booster test on the same driven coil to the 2023 shot, measured, against the change the plant predicts between the 2021 circuit and the 2023 circuit. The plant's own error cancels in that difference to first order. §11 measured the installed filter alone moving the ratio by under 0.90 %, so the move is dominated by the grounding; state that size beside every measured move.

Done when, for every scored shot, the record states:

  • the measured and predicted 6f, 12f and 18f lines on the driven coil and each pickup;
  • the absolute ratio against §9's rule, set beside §9's 2021 result for the same pair;
  • the measured and predicted year move, with the 2021 test it is taken from;
  • a verdict for the claim, judged on the year move: the 2023 design change in filter and grounding predicts the measured move, partly, or not.

A miss in the year move is attributed to the filter, the grounding or the strays, or left unresolved with the deciding measurement named. A miss in the absolute ratio is attributed to the known plant error unless the year move says otherwise. The EF6 arm states both of its scorings and the filter state they favour. Negative control: putting the 2021 grounding (and no filter) in place of the 2023 design moves the predicted lines by the amount the design change implies, and the test fails if it does not. Positive control: the 2021 circuit variant, with the windings' capacitance removed, reproduces a 2021 booster test's recorded §9 ratios, because the composed plant reduces there to the R-L structure §9 scored.

§18 — The 2023 ripple filter in the composed JT-60SA circuits

src/power_convertor/jt60sa_circuits.py reads the register's filter: "booster_ripple" on EF1, EF2, EF5 and EF6, but composes no filter, so every composed booster circuit is unfiltered. Install the 2023 ripple filter on the booster coils from the register's component values, through the filter owner power_convertor.filter_network, with the shunt across the booster branch (shunt_attachment="booster_only", as §11 corrected). Never use the as-drawn attachment. Make the filter a per-coil choice with campaign defaults. A 2021 composition carries no filter, so every stored 2021 comparison scored through the composed circuits reproduces unchanged. A 2023 composition carries it on all four booster coils. A per-coil override removes it from one coil, which is what §17's EF6 arm needs (the 2023 circuit with EF6's filter removed).

Done when the tests show four things. The 2023 booster coil's terminal impedance at 6f and 12f changes with the filter present against removed; the negative control is that removing it must change it. The 2023 composition with EF6's filter overridden off differs from the full 2023 composition at EF6 alone. The as-drawn attachment is refused. The stored 2021 composed residuals reproduce to 1e-9. Write paths: src/power_convertor/jt60sa_circuits.py, tests/test_jt60sa_circuits.py, and the fragment docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/composed-filter.html.

§19 — The 2021 coil-circuit grounding, sourced

The grounding before the alternative grounding system is described in this repository only partly. filter-grounding-prediction calls it single-ended, and its §7 records that the installed supply-side pair was raised to 45 kΩ × 2 from 2.5 kΩ. Start from that value and its source, and find the remaining legs, above all the coil-terminal grounding. The register carries only the 2023 system: the 2 kΩ and 45 kΩ pairs and the 0.6 µF screen. scripts/jt60sa/replay_2021.py uses a stated 1 kΩ receiver shunt with no source. Find the 2021 terminal-to-ground arrangement and its resistances in the JT-60SA documents: the MECS document that gives the 2023 values, the JT-60SA Code wiki on nakasvr26 (fetched as AGENTS.md describes), and the register built by jt60sa-power-supply-sources §3. Record them with citations as a 2021 variant of registers/jt60sa_supplies.json's grounding, refitting nothing.

Done when the 2021 variant is in the register with a citation (document, version and page) for every value, and a test reads it back. Negative control: the read-back test fails when the 2023 grounding values are substituted into the 2021 variant, so an unchanged copy cannot pass for a sourced one. Any leg no document gives is entered in the register as unsourced, with the bounded range §17 will state its year move over as a sensitivity rather than a verdict. The test fails if such a leg carries a single value without a citation. The fragment lists each document and page read. Write paths: src/power_convertor/registers/jt60sa_supplies.json, tests/test_jt60sa_grounding_register.py (its own test file, so it never shares one with §18), and the fragment docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/grounding-2021.html.

For the method carried to ITER:

  • Nova's magnetic coupling stands. It is validated from 0.1 to 30 Hz (§5), on the slow currents (§7) and on fast dumps (§8).
  • At the converter harmonics, most of the measured pickup arrives by a non-magnetic path that grows roughly as √f with a small phase lag.
  • That path is neither the walls (§13), nor the documented terminal circuit (§11), nor the pickup's own supply (§12), nor capacitance to ground or a terminal tap (§14).
  • It cannot be identified from the data and documents held. ITER therefore carries an empirical idle-coil pickup factor and measurement requirements in place of a calibrated harmonic coupling: recorded tap wiring, the inter-coil ground return, a supply-off baseline, and each idle supply's firing state.

jccm-ef1-waveform scores the 2023 dump pickup waveforms in the time domain through terminal_ratio: 18 of 18 pairs on the eight named dumps fit inside the 10% band (EF1->EF6 4.7-7.1%, EF1->EF2 1.9-3.1%, E101079 and E101081 EF6-driven 5.1-6.7%, E101116 and E101117 EF5-driven 2.1-3.6%), the no-passive removal arm is worse on every one, and the complete EF5- and EF6-driven positive control fits, so the section's decision rule resolves the miss the booster tests carry in favour of the tests rather than the hardware; a raw predicted/measured peak shortfall of 70-99% is a ripple spike on the measured channel, reading 96-101% once both peaks are averaged over 5 ms; evidence docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/jccm-ef1-waveform.html, figure docs/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/ef1-waveform/waveform_overlay.svg

§8 closed by its decision rule. Nova's predicted pickup waveforms on the eight 2023 fast discharges fit all 18 pairs within 10 % rms of the measured peak:

  • EF1→EF6 4.7–7.1 %
  • EF1→EF2 1.9–3.1 %
  • EF6-driven 5.1–6.7 %
  • EF5-driven 2.1–3.6 %

The no-passive arm is worse on every pair, and the EF5- and EF6-driven positive control is complete and fits. Both EF1 pairs fit, so the 18.8 % EF1→EF6 miss belongs to the 2021 booster tests, not to a geometry error or a missing conductor. The documented-conductor node is therefore not needed. The 5 ms-smoothed predicted peaks agree at 96–101 %; the raw 70–99 % is ripple on the measured channel. §6 keeps nova below 30 Hz and still takes measured H(f) for EF1→EF6 at the booster harmonics. Merges 5721dc1 and b6c03e1. evidence

Independent review of c9993b8e3a4c2248b8651b705cd01846534b17bb records six parsed scores, 2 follow-on findings and an unmeasured added-failure count because the reviewed base log was not a suite arm.

<a href="/power_convertor/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/jccm-harmonic-nova.html#jccm-harmonic-nova-results">Harmonic nova result</a>: 52 reproduced lines, 0/26 at 6f, 0/19 at 12f, 0/7 at 18f within the joint band; <a href="/power_convertor/figures/jt60sa-coil-circuit-model/harmonic-nova/ratios.svg">amplitude and phase figure</a>.

§9 closed with a negative result. Nominal nova fits none of the 52 measured harmonic line ratios: 0/26 at 6f, 0/19 at 12f and 0/7 at 18f. It over-screens by a median 80–93 % in amplitude, while M/L under-screens. No error band can be carried to ITER from this section, and the ITER coordinator marks its ripple results provisional until the cause is found.

Candidates:

  • wall currents not resolved through the thickness;
  • 3D eddy paths;
  • pickup loading;
  • a coil-terminal resonance;
  • a non-inductive path, for the three opposite-side lines.

The lead added three follow-ups on 2026-10-15: a skin-effect check, walls resolved in nova, and the 2023 filter and grounding circuit. Nova's layered-wall option (nova 207a66408) already exists from the ITER coordinator's passive-skin-effect node, and on ITER it moves coil coupling by under 1 % at 300–1600 Hz. The JT-60SA re-score with layered walls is the direct test. Merge 3a5647a. evidence

Correction to c-close-s9. The ITER figure of “under 1 %” compared two resolved meshes, 6 mm against 12 mm face strips. It does not compare layered walls with the one-layer plant. The ITER coordinator's later comparison of layered walls with the present one-layer plant lowers coil-to-coil transfer by up to about 5 % at 300–1600 Hz, which is more screening, and two and four layers agree to four decimals. Constraining each source wall to one uniform current lowers it by up to about 6 % more. §10 states the corrected figure.

The lead funded §16 on 21 October 2026 because JT-60SA's EF windings are built like ITER's PF windings, so the verdict transfers. Gate g-jccm-5 passes on shared-coil-supply-model §3's landing. The node first reruns the derived JT-60SA plant caches on the regenerated thick-coil matrices (b89fdb0f), then scores the six rising pairs under cross-validation. The 2021 data are held, so no site access is needed.

§17 closed. The registered 2023 filter and grounding do not account for the measured 2021-to-2023 move of the coil-to-coil lines.

  • 7 of 120 lines fall within the rule, with a median error of 90.3 %.
  • The predicted move is about 0.93 on every line; the measured move runs from 0.08× to 74×.
  • A no-change prediction brings 3 lines within the rule, so the stored verdict reads “partly” by that comparison.
  • EF6's 2023 filter state cannot be separated.

For ITER this supports keeping harmonic idle-coil coupling empirical, with measurement requirements. The follow-on batch has also landed (e54e8502). Merges 22fa0d89 and e54e8502. evidence
